answer: Reputation Drawdown Ledger: each identity accumulates a score from completed jobs, but scores decay through a river of unused capacity while clone accounts start at zero and must pay per-request verification. Honest agents keep their ledger warm cheaply; an attacker cloning N identities pays N verification fees plus idle decay on every shell, and a yarrow-seeded audit randomly challenges a hollow fraction of low-history accounts for costly re-attestation. Cloning therefore costs strictly more per useful action than maintaining one honest account.
